raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Purpose

Fixes #52710.

The DeepSeek V4 compressor imported the optional CUDA CuTe DSL implementation
unconditionally for `head_dim == 512`. Builds without CuTe DSL therefore failed
at dispatch.

The fallback must also respect the cache layout. The Triton compressor writes
the packed `fp8_ds_mla` representation (`torch.uint8`); it is not compatible
with FlashInfer's plain BF16 or per-tensor FP8 cache rows. This change therefore:

- uses CuTe DSL when it is available on CUDA;
- permits the Triton fallback only for packed `torch.uint8` cache rows; and
- raises a clear error for plain BF16/per-tensor FP8 rows without CuTe DSL.

## Duplicate-work check

No open PR addresses this issue.

## Test Plan

- Execute `DeepseekCompressor.forward` with CuTe DSL unavailable for packed
  `uint8`, plain BF16, and plain FP8 E4M3 cache rows.
- Assert the plain layouts fail before the Triton callable can launch.
- Assert the packed layout dispatches to Triton.
- On SM89+, execute the real packed Triton writer against a 584-byte cache row
  followed by a sentinel guard region and verify the guard is unchanged.
- Run the Python-specific pre-commit lint and formatting hooks.

## Test Result

- RTX 3050 (SM86), driver 610.88, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130:
  - plain BF16 forward rejection: **passed**
  - plain FP8 E4M3 forward rejection: **passed**
  - packed `uint8` forward dispatch: **passed**
  - real packed FP8 write with overrun sentinel: **skipped**, because native
    FP8 E4M3 conversion requires SM89+
- Focused pytest result: **3 passed, 1 skipped**
- Kaggle probe: Tesla P100 (SM60), also below the SM89 requirement
- `pre-commit run ruff-check --files ...`: **passed**
- `pre-commit run ruff-format --files ...`: **passed**
- `git diff origin/main...HEAD --check`: **passed**

The SM89+-gated sentinel test is included for Ada/Hopper/Blackwell CI.

## Model evaluation

Not run. This change does not modify model math, kernels, output values, or model
loading. It restricts dispatch according to the existing cache representation
and prevents an incompatible writer from receiving plain cache rows.

No documentation update is needed because this fixes internal optional-kernel
dispatch without changing the public interface.

AI assistance was used for the implementation. I reviewed every change.

- Platform/build: SystemPanic/vllm-windows
- GPU: NVIDIA H200, sm_90a
- OS: Windows

- Model runner: V2
- Configured KV-cache dtype: `fp8`
- Block size: 256
- Speculative decoding: DSpark with 7 speculative tokens

CuTe DSL is not available in this build. This was verified directly:

```text
vLLM: 0.25.1.dev14+g169a4cbe6
has_cutedsl: False
```

### Resolved cache layout and attention backend

The server follows the DeepSeek V4 H200 recipe and is configured with:

```text
--kv-cache-dtype fp8
```

The startup log confirms that DeepSeek V4 resolves this internally to the packed `fp8_ds_mla` cache format:

```text
[attention.py:91] Using DeepSeek's fp8_ds_mla KV cache format.
[attention.py:694] Using FP8 indexer cache for Lightning Indexer.
[flashinfer_sparse_mla_warmup.py:233] Warming up DeepSeek V4 sparse MLA attention for mixed tokens=16.
```

Therefore, the relevant configuration is:

```text
Configured KV-cache dtype: fp8
Resolved cache layout: fp8_ds_mla
Sparse MLA attention backend: FlashInfer
CuTe DSL available: no
```

### Result with the local `has_cutedsl()` guard

With CuTe DSL unavailable and the local guard applied:

- Model initialization succeeds.
- KV-cache allocation and sparse MLA warmup succeed.
- The existing Triton compressor fallback is selected instead of the CuTe DSL path.
- Compressor forward succeeds during inference.
- End-to-end Chat Completions requests return HTTP 200.
- Token generation completes successfully.
- No incompatible cache-writer error or apparent cache corruption has been observed.

Example runtime evidence:

```text
POST /v1/chat/completions HTTP/1.1" 200 OK
Engine 000: Avg generation throughput: 30.1 tokens/s
```

This supports the intended packed `fp8_ds_mla` fallback case on H200. Although the configured CLI value is `fp8`, vLLM resolves it to DeepSeek's packed `fp8_ds_mla` cache layout before inference.

detail.body:
## Purpose

Fixes #52710.

The DeepSeek V4 compressor imported the optional CUDA CuTe DSL implementation
unconditionally for `head_dim == 512`. Builds without CuTe DSL therefore failed
at dispatch.

The fallback must also respect the cache layout. The Triton compressor writes
the packed `fp8_ds_mla` representation (`torch.uint8`); it is not compatible
with FlashInfer's plain BF16 or per-tensor FP8 cache rows. This change therefore:

- uses CuTe DSL when it is available on CUDA;
- permits the Triton fallback only for packed `torch.uint8` cache rows; and
- raises a clear error for plain BF16/per-tensor FP8 rows without CuTe DSL.

## Duplicate-work check

No open PR addresses this issue.

## Test Plan

- Execute `DeepseekCompressor.forward` with CuTe DSL unavailable for packed
  `uint8`, plain BF16, and plain FP8 E4M3 cache rows.
- Assert the plain layouts fail before the Triton callable can launch.
- Assert the packed layout dispatches to Triton.
- On SM89+, execute the real packed Triton writer against a 584-byte cache row
  followed by a sentinel guard region and verify the guard is unchanged.
- Run the Python-specific pre-commit lint and formatting hooks.

## Test Result

- RTX 3050 (SM86), driver 610.88, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130:
  - plain BF16 forward rejection: **passed**
  - plain FP8 E4M3 forward rejection: **passed**
  - packed `uint8` forward dispatch: **passed**
  - real packed FP8 write with overrun sentinel: **skipped**, because native
    FP8 E4M3 conversion requires SM89+
- Focused pytest result: **3 passed, 1 skipped**
- Kaggle probe: Tesla P100 (SM60), also below the SM89 requirement
- `pre-commit run ruff-check --files ...`: **passed**
- `pre-commit run ruff-format --files ...`: **passed**
- `git diff origin/main...HEAD --check`: **passed**

The SM89+-gated sentinel test is included for Ada/Hopper/Blackwell CI.

## Model evaluation

Not run. This change does not modify model math, kernels, output values, or model
loading. It restricts dispatch according to the existing cache representation
and prevents an incompatible writer from receiving plain cache rows.

No documentation update is needed because this fixes internal optional-kernel
dispatch without changing the public interface.

AI assistance was used for the implementation. I reviewed every change.

@@ -42,6 +43,21 @@ def _prefer_two_stage_compressor() -> bool:
     return current_platform.is_rocm()
 
 
+def _use_cutedsl_compressor(head_dim: int, kv_cache_dtype: torch.dtype) -> bool:
+    if head_dim != 512:
+        return False
+    if current_platform.is_cuda() and has_cutedsl():
+        return True
+    if kv_cache_dtype != torch.uint8:
+        raise RuntimeError(
+            "DeepSeek V4 plain BF16/per-tensor FP8 KV cache compression "
+            "requires the CuTe DSL compressor, but CuTe DSL is unavailable. "
+            "The Triton fallback only supports the packed fp8_ds_mla "
+            "torch.uint8 layout."
+        )
+    return False
+
+

     seq_lens_cpu = metadata.seq_lens_cpu_upper_bound
     if seq_lens_cpu is None:
@@ -444,7 +460,7 @@ def forward(
         # cutedsl (head=512) accepts the full-cache flags; triton (indexer/AMD)
         # does not, so the two callables have different signatures.
         compress_norm_rope_store_fn: Any
-        if current_platform.is_cuda() and self.head_dim == 512:
+        if _use_cutedsl_compressor(self.head_dim, kv_cache.dtype):
             from .nvidia.ops.sparse_attn_compress_cutedsl import (

@rogeroberg, could you please verify whether #52742 fixes this on your H200 build without CuTe DSL? The revised fix is cache-layout aware: it allows the Triton fallback only for packed fp8_ds_mla / torch.uint8 rows, while plain BF16 or per-tensor FP8 rows fail clearly instead of invoking an incompatible writer. If possible, please share the attention backend / kv-cache dtype used and whether the compressor forward succeeds on your setup.

Hi  @maithilijoshi20,  

Thanks for the update. I am currently using the SystemPanic/vllm-windows build, so I cant run the fix diretly in my environment. see below for some additional details though:

"I can provide results from my H200 Windows setup using the simpler local patch suggested in the original report:

```python
if (
    current_platform.is_cuda()
    and self.head_dim == 512
    and has_cutedsl()
):
```

### Environment

- Platform/build: SystemPanic/vllm-windows
- GPU: NVIDIA H200, sm_90a
- OS: Windows
- vLLM: `0.25.1.dev14+g169a4cbe6`
- Model: `DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731`
- Tensor parallel size: 4
- Expert parallelism: enabled
- Model runner: V2
- Configured KV-cache dtype: `fp8`
- Block size: 256
- Speculative decoding: DSpark with 7 speculative tokens

CuTe DSL is not available in this build. This was verified directly:

```text
vLLM: 0.25.1.dev14+g169a4cbe6
has_cutedsl: False
```

### Resolved cache layout and attention backend

The server follows the DeepSeek V4 H200 recipe and is configured with:

```text
--kv-cache-dtype fp8
```

The startup log confirms that DeepSeek V4 resolves this internally to the packed `fp8_ds_mla` cache format:

```text
[attention.py:91] Using DeepSeek's fp8_ds_mla KV cache format.
[attention.py:694] Using FP8 indexer cache for Lightning Indexer.
[flashinfer_sparse_mla_warmup.py:233] Warming up DeepSeek V4 sparse MLA attention for mixed tokens=16.
```

Therefore, the relevant configuration is:

```text
Configured KV-cache dtype: fp8
Resolved cache layout: fp8_ds_mla
Sparse MLA attention backend: FlashInfer
CuTe DSL available: no
```

### Result with the local `has_cutedsl()` guard

With CuTe DSL unavailable and the local guard applied:

- Model initialization succeeds.
- KV-cache allocation and sparse MLA warmup succeed.
- The existing Triton compressor fallback is selected instead of the CuTe DSL path.
- Compressor forward succeeds during inference.
- End-to-end Chat Completions requests return HTTP 200.
- Token generation completes successfully.
- No incompatible cache-writer error or apparent cache corruption has been observed.

Example runtime evidence:

```text
POST /v1/chat/completions HTTP/1.1" 200 OK
Engine 000: Avg generation throughput: 30.1 tokens/s
```

This supports the intended packed `fp8_ds_mla` fallback case on H200. Although the configured CLI value is `fp8`, vLLM resolves it to DeepSeek's packed `fp8_ds_mla` cache layout before inference.
